questions.q: What is the first step of risk management?
questions.explain: You start by identifying assets, their owners, threats, and vulnerabilities. Without an inventory, the analysis has no foundation.

questions.q: What is the role of a risk register?
options: Document each risk, its owner, score, treatment, and review
questions.explain: The register is a living tool for tracking and communication. Each row has an owner and a review date.

questions.q: Which analysis method uses a likelihood × impact matrix?
questions.explain: A matrix and low/medium/high scales belong to qualitative analysis. Quantitative analysis uses monetary values (SLE, ALE).

questions.q: An asset is worth €100,000. An incident destroys 40% of its value. What is the SLE?
questions.explain: SLE = Asset Value × EF = 100,000 × 0.4 = €40,000. EF describes the magnitude of loss for a single event.

questions.q: An asset is worth €200,000. An incident destroys 25% of its value and occurs twice a year. What is the ALE?
An incident occurs on average once every five years. What is the ARO?
questions.explain: ARO = number of events per year. Once every five years = 1/5 = 0.2.

questions.q: A control costs €25,000/year and reduces ALE from €30,000 to €8,000. What can be concluded?
options: The control is cost-effective: it saves €30,000
The control is not cost-effective as-is: it saves €22,000 for a cost of €25,000
The control is cost-effective: it saves €8,000
You cannot compare a cost and an ALE
questions.explain: Savings = 30,000 − 8,000 = €22,000/year, which is less than the €25,000 cost. You should negotiate, choose another control, or accept the risk with documentation.

questions.q: A company purchases cyber insurance. Which risk treatment is it applying?
questions.explain: Insurance transfers part of the financial loss to a third party. It does not remove legal responsibility or reputational risk.

questions.q: An organization decides to stop collecting data it does not need. Which risk treatment is this?
questions.explain: Eliminating the risky activity is avoidance. Data minimization is a form of structural avoidance.

questions.q: After deploying controls, a risk drops from a score of 20 to 6 out of 25. What is the score of 6 called?
questions.explain: The score remaining after controls is residual risk. It must be formally accepted by an authority.

The maximum tolerable loss for a service
The number of incidents per year
questions.explain: Appetite is a leadership decision, translated into thresholds. Maximum tolerable downtime relates to MTD in a BIA.

questions.q: In a BIA, what does RTO represent?
options: Target time to restore the service
questions.explain: RTO = Recovery Time Objective, the target time to restore service. RPO is acceptable data loss; MTD is maximum tolerable downtime.

questions.q: Which relationship must always hold between RTO and MTD?
questions.explain: Recovery must be faster than the maximum tolerable downtime. RTO < MTD, otherwise continuity planning is flawed.

questions.q: Match each risk treatment to its example.

pairs.right: Assume a low risk, documented and reviewed

questions.explain: All four treatments can coexist. Acceptance must be authorized and dated; transfer does not eliminate reputational risk.

questions.q: Which statements about quantitative analysis are accurate? (Select all that apply)
options: It expresses risk in monetary value
It allows comparing risk to the cost of a control
It requires reliable historical data to be credible
questions.explain: Quantitative analysis provides comparable figures, but relies on assumptions and data. It is never free of uncertainty.
